conviction_note: The 20-day -25.7% drawdown is documented sector/rate beta rather than company news, and the one thing I could observe that no aggregator carries -- Torrington staffing a full second and third shift right now -- points the other way to the +11.6-point put skew; I net a small positive (+2.0 hiring, +0.8 insider buy, -1.5 stalled Fit conversion) and keep it far inside the 10.36% implied move because the printed P&L on a -16% revenue quarter is genuinely likely to be ugly.

findings.finding: FuelCell's own careers site right now shows 61 of its 80 open requisitions at the Torrington cell plant and, critically, an entire third shift being staffed end-to-end -- Supervisor Tape Casting (Third Shift), Sheet Metal Supervisor (Third Shift), Warehouse Supervisor (Third Shift), Material Handler (Third Shift), QA Inspector Manufacturing (Third Shift), EH&S Specialist (Third Shift), Facility Tech (Third Shift), Janitor (Third Shift) and Security Officer (3rd Shift), plus a parallel second-shift set -- i.e. a 24/7 line being commissioned, not incremental backfill.
findings.why_not_priced: Management explicitly declined to give a current annualised production rate on the 8 June call, so the only public number is the aspiration (500 MW/yr, $200-275m, 24 months). Nobody aggregates shift designations in job postings. If the market had this, the mid-August coverage would be arguing about output cadence and the $213m raise as pre-funded plant capex; instead the wire copy is 'dilution concerns tied to the $225m July offering' and rate-driven risk-off, and 25-delta puts would not be bid 11.6 vol points over calls on a name whose plant is hiring janitors and security guards for a third shift. Third-shift support functions are the cheapest possible tell that the shift is actually being run, because no one hires a 3am janitor speculatively.
findings.independence: Different document, same direction: on the Q2 call management raised the Torrington target from 350 MW to 500 MW/yr at $200-275m over 24 months and said capital was already allocated for long-lead equipment -- the hiring is that plan being executed on schedule. https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-fuelcell-energys-q2-2026-sees-revenue-dip-5-93CH-4731028 (2026-06-08). Note the rejobs.org mirror of the Third Shift Facility Tech posting is the same underlying requisition, not an independent observation.

findings.finding: Homer John Livingston III, who only became a FuelCell director on 19 May 2026, bought 26,343 shares in the open market on 16 July 2026 at a weighted-average $18.79 (about $495k, transaction code P, direct) -- an actual cash purchase at a company where every other recent insider line is a director-fee stock grant or a 10b5-1 sale.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed on 20 July into the middle of the sector de-rating and the stock has fallen another 11% since, so it plainly did not set the price; a market that had weighted it would not be paying an 11.6-point put skew nine days before the print. The signal is the contrast, and the contrast requires reading three separate accessions in the same week rather than a headline: the two Form 4s filed 16 July are zero-price director-fee deferred stock units (Livingston 833 units, Hansen 988 units) and the 6 July Form 4 is an EVP selling 2,500 shares at $28.71 under a plan adopted in January. A buy at $18.79 by a nine-week-old director is the only discretionary cash commitment in the file.
findings.independence: Separate accession confirming he is newly seated (Form 3, event date 19 May 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000089706926001390/form3.xml . The contrasting 10b5-1 sale is a different accession again: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000089706926001496/form4.xml

findings.finding: The Fit Energy CEPA's only alignment mechanism -- 12,000,000 warrant shares in three 4m tranches, each vesting only on FuelCell receiving a non-refundable deposit equal to 16% of the order value for the next 100 MW -- is struck at $26.44, now 58% above the $16.72 spot, and in the ten weeks since signing there has been no 8-K, no press release, no named data-centre site and no phase election; FuelCell's press-release feed shows nothing operational since 9 July, against management's own commitment to convert submitted proposals into contracted backlog 'within this fiscal year' (FY ends 31 October).
findings.why_not_priced: The 54% drawdown from the 52-week high does price 'Fit optionality is worth less', which is why I size this small and negative-but-modest rather than large. What is not priced is the specific mechanism: only Phase 0 (30 MW) is committed, Phases 1-3 (350 MW) are at Fit's sole option, and the consideration FuelCell offered Fit for electing them is now deep out-of-the-money paper with a hard 24-month vesting cliff from 22 June 2026. If the market had modelled that, the sell-side previews would be framing 2 September as a Phase-1-election checkpoint rather than an EPS event, and there would be visible commentary on Fit Energy USA LP itself -- a Boca Raton vehicle whose named CEO, Joel Leonoff, comes from payments, not power, and which has issued nothing of its own since 24 June.
findings.independence: Same source cluster, flagged: the 424B7 registering the 12,000,000 warrant shares for resale (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/886128/000110465926085425/tm2616970-5_424b7.htm, 2026-07-21) is a second reading of the same warrant, so it should collapse into this finding. Genuinely separate: the company's own press-release index showing only three releases since May, the last operational one dated 9 July -- https://investor.fce.com/press-releases/default.aspx (2026-09-01).

searched_and_found_nothing: A new ATM or equity distribution agreement under the 8 June 2026 S-3ASR automatic shelf: the only 424 filed since is the 21 July 424B7, which is a resale registration for Fit Energy's warrant shares and raises nothing for the company; no sales agreement exhibit found

Share count uncertainty: fully resolved from the final 424B5, 78,322,459 shares outstanding after the $21.00 offering (79,929,602 on full greenshoe) versus 67,608,173 at 30 June -- no unsourced gap left to hunt (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000886128/000110465926081853/tm2616970-3_424b5.htm)
Any Fit Energy project trail: no air permit, interconnection queue entry, site, utility filing or named data-centre offtaker found in any state

A repeat of the Q2 $42.6m Groton impairment: the CEO said on the 8 June call that the SureSource 4000 units at Groton are the only ones of that platform in the fleet and the rest of the portfolio already runs the standard block, so I could not build a further-impairment thesis

Korean customer or policy distress: the EXIM first tranche for the five 2.8 MW blocks to Gyeonggi Green Energy was scheduled to disburse 30 June 2026, inside Q3, with a second tranche in October, and I found nothing adverse
Form 4 cluster around the July offering: mostly routine director-fee deferred stock units plus one 2,500-share 10b5-1 sale by an EVP at $28.71; only one real purchase

Hartford Business Journal 'FuelCell ramps up Torr'ton output, jobs' -- discarded on date grounds. Its numbers (295 headcount, 600 employees worldwide, 70 MW output, a planned 14.9 MW Bridgeport fuel-cell park) belong to a much older article served against a 2026 query; it is not evidence about the current ramp and I did not use it
baseline_tension: My primary finding cuts against the baseline -- the +11.6-point put skew and the 25.7% twenty-day drawdown say downside, while the plant is visibly staffing a third shift and a new director wrote a $495k cheque at $18.79 -- and the one finding that agrees with the skew (the stalled Fit phase conversion) I have deliberately sized small precisely because a 54% decline from the high has already had a lot of that.
